You get a straight answer, whether or not you work with us.</p> <div class="acts" style="margin-top:24px"><a class="btn btn-p" href="https://www.encloud9.com/lp/schedule-a-meeting/">Book a call</a><a class="lnk" href="tel:+18442640729">1-844-264-0729 <span>→</span></a></div> </div> <div class="faq rev"> <details><summary>How much does Dynamics 365 cost?

Microsoft list prices for Dynamics 365 Sales are $65, $105 or $150 per user per month, paid yearly. Accelerators are $7,500, a full implementation starts at $20,000, and Rescue and Repair runs $500 to $10,000, each confirmed in writing. Support starts at $500 a month. See our pricing guide.From Home →

How long does a Dynamics 365 setup take?

Our accelerators take [Brian sets] weeks. On our 9 published projects with a delivery time, go-live took 1 to 6 months, and 7 of the 9 took three months or less. You get the plan, with dates, before we build.From Home →

Can you take over a system another partner built?

Yes. Rescue and Repair is for Dynamics 365 systems that are over-customized, stalled or out of date. We review it first and tell you what to keep.From Home →

Is Copilot included with Dynamics 365?

Copilot is built into Dynamics 365 Sales Enterprise and Premium. Agents run on Copilot Credits, which most plans buy separately. We tell you what it costs to run before anything is switched on.From Home →

What is a generative page?

A page in your Dynamics 365 app that is built from a plain-words request, such as a report on deals that have gone quiet. It runs inside your Dynamics 365 app, on your live records.From Home →

aria-labelledby="fit-h"> <div class="fitsplit"> <div class="side rev"> <h2 class="h2" id="fit-h">What does Microsoft cover for health data?</h2> <p class="lead">Microsoft offers a HIPAA Business Associate Agreement that covers Dynamics 365, Power Apps, Power Automate and Power BI. It does not make you compliant on its own: your setup, security roles and processes still have to meet HIPAA.</p> <div class="acts" style="margin-top:0"><a class="btn btn-p" href="https://www.encloud9.com/lp/schedule-a-meeting/">Book a call</a></div> </div> <div class="fit rev"> <div class="yes"><h3 class="h3">From Microsoft</h3><ul> <li>Dynamics 365, Power Apps, Power Automate and Power BI are in scope for Microsoft's HIPAA Business Associate Agreement.</li> <li>The agreement comes with Microsoft's Data Protection Addendum by default for customers who are covered entities or business associates.</li> <li>Microsoft says a BAA supports your HIPAA compliance but does not achieve it on its own.</li> <li>Read it on <a class="lnk" href="https://learn.microsoft.com/compliance/regulatory/offering-hipaa-hitech">Microsoft Learn</a>.</li> </ul></div> </div> </div> </section> <section class="sec" id="faq" aria-labelledby="fq-h"> <div class="faqsplit"> <div class="faqside rev"> <h2 class="h2" id="fq-h">Healthcare questions we get asked</h2> <p class="lead" style="margin-top:18px">Something else on your mind? Microsoft includes Dynamics 365 in its HIPAA Business Associate Agreement. Using it does not make you compliant on its own; your setup, access rules and processes have to meet HIPAA too.From Healthcare →

Do we need to sign a BAA with Microsoft?

Microsoft makes its HIPAA Business Associate Agreement available by default through its Data Protection Addendum to customers who are covered entities or business associates.From Healthcare →

Does enCloud9 sign a BAA with clients?

[Brian confirms.]From Healthcare →

Which Dynamics 365 apps do healthcare clients use?

Our healthcare and compliance clients run Dynamics 365 Sales, and some add Customer Service. Power Apps, Power Automate and Power BI extend them on the same data.From Healthcare →

Can you fix a healthcare CRM another partner built?

Yes. enCloud9 takes over systems other partners built, finds what is broken, and fixes it in priority order. See Rescue and Repair.From Healthcare →

Can Dynamics 365 handle several divisions?

Can you connect Dynamics 365 to our other systems?

Yes. enCloud9 builds Dynamics 365 for small and mid-sized businesses, and distributors are one of the industries we lead with.From Distribution →

Can our sellers see stock and credit in Dynamics 365?

Yes, if you run Business Central. Microsoft's integration shows item availability, price lists, balances and open invoices in Dynamics 365 Sales. See the Business Central integration.From Distribution →

What if we run a different ERP?

Tell us what you run and we will tell you what the link takes. Other connections can be built with Power Automate or custom work, quoted in writing.From Distribution →

Can Dynamics 365 handle returns?

Yes. Dynamics 365 Customer Service tracks each return or question as a case, with queues and service levels, so nothing sits in one inbox.From Distribution →

Pick the app that matches the work you want to fix first: selling, service, phone and chat, field visits, marketing or projects. Most growing businesses start with Dynamics 365 Sales, Customer Service or both, and add the others when the work calls for them.From Dynamics 365 →

How much does Dynamics 365 cost?

Microsoft list prices start at $50 to $65 per user per month and go to $150 to $195 for premium plans, paid yearly. Accelerators are $7,500, a full implementation starts at $20,000, and Rescue and Repair runs $500 to $10,000, each confirmed in writing. Support starts at $500 a month. See our Dynamics 365 pricing guide.From Dynamics 365 →

Can one person use two Dynamics 365 apps?

Yes. Each full user gets one base license for the highest-priced app they need, plus a lower-priced attach license for each extra app. People who only read records or enter time can use the lower-cost Team Members license.From Dynamics 365 →

Do we need a support plan after go-live?

Yes. New clients start on at least the Stability plan, $500 a month for 4 hours, on a 12-month agreement. Monthly plans include a 1-hour response during business hours, 7:00am to 5:00pm Central, Monday to Friday.From Dynamics 365 →

Ask us on a call. You get a straight answer, whether or not you work with us.</p> <div class="acts" style="margin-top:24px"><a class="btn btn-p" href="https://www.encloud9.com/lp/schedule-a-meeting/">Book a call</a><a class="lnk" href="tel:+18442640729">1-844-264-0729 <span>→</span></a></div> </div> <div> <div class="faq rev"> <details><summary>How much does Dynamics 365 Sales cost?

Microsoft's list price is $65, $105 or $150 per user per month, paid yearly, for Sales Professional, Enterprise or Premium. Setup is a separate project, quoted in writing after a short call, and support plans start at $500 a month. Agents can add Copilot Credit costs, which we estimate before you switch them on.From Dynamics 365 Sales →

How long does a Dynamics 365 Sales implementation take?

The Sales Accelerator takes [Brian sets] weeks. On our 9 published projects with a delivery time, go-live took 1 to 6 months, and 7 of the 9 took three months or less. The Schiff Group went live on a new Dynamics 365 Sales system in one month.From Dynamics 365 Sales →

Do we need Sales Professional, Enterprise or Premium?

Most B2B sales teams start with Sales Enterprise, because it adds Copilot, forecasting and territory management to the core CRM. Professional suits small teams that need core pipeline tracking without Copilot. Premium suits teams that plan to run agents at volume, since it includes 1,000 Copilot Credits per user per month.From Dynamics 365 Sales →

Is Copilot included in Dynamics 365 Sales?

Copilot in Dynamics 365 Sales, Outlook and Teams is included in Sales Enterprise and Sales Premium, not in Sales Professional. The Sales agents are available on all three plans but run on Copilot Credits. Only Sales Premium includes credits; on other plans you buy them separately.From Dynamics 365 Sales →

What do the Sales agents cost to run?

Agents use Copilot Credits for each answer and action. Microsoft sells credits in packs of 25,000 for $200 a month, or pay-as-you-go through an Azure subscription. We estimate your monthly use with Microsoft's estimator and set a spending limit before an agent goes live.From Dynamics 365 Sales →

Can you fix a Dynamics 365 Sales system another partner built?

Yes. Our Rescue and Repair package takes over systems that are over-customized, stalled or out of date, and takes them back to standard where it can. Tension Envelope's stalled project from a prior partner was back on track within three months.From Dynamics 365 Sales →

Can you move our data from Salesforce, HubSpot or spreadsheets?

Yes. Moving data from your old CRM or spreadsheets is part of a full implementation, and the Sales Accelerator includes an import of up to [Brian sets] records. Integrations with other systems are quoted separately.From Dynamics 365 Sales →

You get a straight answer, whether or not you work with us.</p> <div class="acts" style="margin-top:24px"><a class="btn btn-p" href="https://www.encloud9.com/lp/schedule-a-meeting/">Book a call</a><a class="lnk" href="tel:+18442640729">1-844-264-0729 <span>→</span></a></div> </div> <div class="faq rev"> <details><summary>How much does Dynamics 365 Customer Service cost?

Microsoft's list price is $50, $105 or $195 per user per month, paid yearly, for Customer Service Professional, Enterprise or Premium. Setup is a separate project, quoted in writing after a short call, and support plans start at $500 a month. Agents can add Copilot Credit costs, which we estimate before you switch them on.From Customer Service →

How long does a Dynamics 365 Customer Service implementation take?

The Service Accelerator takes [Brian sets] weeks. On our 9 published projects with a delivery time, go-live took 1 to 6 months, and 7 of the 9 took three months or less.From Customer Service →

Do we need Customer Service Professional, Enterprise or Premium?

Professional covers cases and the knowledge base, without Copilot. Enterprise adds Copilot in Customer Service, unified routing, Teams integration, analytics and KPI reporting, and workflow automation. Premium adds chatbots, live chat, a voice channel and base Copilot Credit capacity for the service agents.From Customer Service →

Is Copilot included in Dynamics 365 Customer Service?

Copilot in Customer Service is included in Customer Service Enterprise and Premium, not in Customer Service Professional. The Case Management, Customer Intent, Customer Knowledge Management and Quality Evaluation agents run on Copilot Credits. Premium includes base Copilot Credit capacity for them; on other plans you buy credits separately. Some agents, including the Case Management and Customer Intent agents, also need a pay-as-you-go plan on an Azure subscription.From Customer Service →

Does Customer Service Professional include service-level agreements?

Yes. Microsoft's documentation lists service-level agreements for Customer Service Professional and Enterprise. You cannot mix Professional and Enterprise users in one environment.From Customer Service →

Does Dynamics 365 Customer Service include phone and chat?

Live chat and a voice channel come with Customer Service Premium. Azure Communication Services pricing is separate and not included. Dynamics 365 Contact Center is a separate product at $110 per user per month, paid yearly. The Service Accelerator does not include channel setup; we quote that work separately.From Customer Service →

Can you fix a Dynamics 365 Customer Service system another partner built?

Yes. Our Rescue and Repair package takes over systems that are over-customized, stalled or out of date, and takes them back to standard where it can.From Customer Service →

Can you move our cases and contacts from another help desk or spreadsheets?

Yes. The Service Accelerator includes an import of up to [Brian sets] records. Moving data from several systems is part of a full implementation. Integrations with other systems are quoted separately.From Customer Service →

How much does Dynamics 365 cost per user?

At Microsoft list price, paid yearly, Dynamics 365 Sales runs $65 to $150 per user per month, Customer Service $50 to $195, Field Service $105 and Project Operations $135. Customer Insights is priced per company, from $1,000 a month with attach pricing.From Dynamics 365 pricing →

What is the cheapest Dynamics 365 license?

For full users, Customer Service Professional and Field Service Contractor are the lowest listed prices at $50 per user per month. For light users, the Team Members license costs less; ask us for the current price.From Dynamics 365 pricing →

Can I pay for Dynamics 365 monthly?

Yes. Microsoft's listed prices are for paying yearly. Paying monthly on an annual subscription costs 5% more, a rule Microsoft has applied since 1 April 2025.From Dynamics 365 pricing →

Is there a minimum number of users?

Most apps have no minimum on Microsoft's pricing pages. Microsoft Relationship Sales needs 10 seats, and Customer Insights Attach needs 10 or more users of a qualifying Dynamics 365 app.From Dynamics 365 pricing →

What does setup cost?

Accelerators are $7,500 fixed, a full implementation starts at $20,000, and Rescue and Repair runs $500 to $10,000, each quoted in writing. Microsoft licenses are a separate cost, and support plans start at $500 a month.From Dynamics 365 pricing →

365 licenses are there?</h2> <p class="lead">Three license types decide most of the bill: base, attach and Team Members. Power Apps use rights, Copilot Credits and storage come with them or on top.</p> </div> <div class="tbl-wrap rev" tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="Table, scrolls sideways on small screens"> <table class="tbl"> <caption class="mono" style="text-align:left;padding-bottom:10px">Dynamics 365 license types</caption> <thead><tr><th scope="col">License</th><th scope="col">Who it is for</th><th scope="col">What to know</th></tr></thead> <tbody> <tr><th scope="row">Base license</th><td data-l="Who it is for">Every full user</td><td data-l="What to know">One per user, for the highest-priced app that person needs</td></tr> <tr><th scope="row">Attach license</th><td data-l="Who it is for">A full user who needs a second app</td><td data-l="What to know">Lower price than a second full license</td></tr> <tr><th scope="row">Team Members</th><td data-l="Who it is for">People who view records, enter time or update their own items</td><td data-l="What to know">Set apps only, and up to 15 tables in a custom app; price from your partner or the Microsoft 365 admin center</td></tr> <tr><th scope="row">Power Apps use rights</th><td data-l="Who it is for">Full Dynamics 365 users</td><td data-l="What to know">Covers apps that extend the licensed app, in the same environment; stricter checks from February 2027</td></tr> <tr><th scope="row">Copilot Credits</th><td data-l="Who it is for">Companies that run agents</td><td data-l="What to know">Sales Premium includes 1,000 per user per month; others buy packs or pay as they go</td></tr> <tr><th scope="row">Storage</th><td data-l="Who it is for">Every company</td><td data-l="What to know">Default storage grows with full licenses; extra database storage is $40 per GB per month</td></tr> </tbody> </table> <p class="fine">From Microsoft Learn and Microsoft's pricing pages, checked 4 and 9 Nov 2026. <a class="lnk" href="nine-blog-pricing-2026.html">Full 2026 price list and licensing guide</a></p> </div> </section> <section class="sec" id="fit" aria-labelledby="fit-h"> <div class="fitsplit"> <div class="side rev"> <h2 class="h2" id="fit-h">How do we know our licenses are right?</h2> <p class="lead">Most waste comes from two mistakes: full licenses for people who only need Team Members, and two full licenses where one base plus an attach would do. Book a call and we go through your users, apps and storage with you.</p> <div class="acts" style="margin-top:0"><a class="btn btn-p" href="https://www.encloud9.com/lp/schedule-a-meeting/">Book a call</a></div> </div> <div class="fit rev"> <div class="yes"><h3 class="h3">Time for a check if</h3><ul> <li>Some users only view records or enter time, but have full licenses.</li> <li>One person holds two full licenses for two apps.</li> <li>Your storage is near 100%. Past that, Microsoft blocks new environments, and sandboxes lock after 30 and 90 days. See <a class="lnk" href="nine-storage.html">storage</a>.</li> <li>You run custom apps outside a Dynamics 365 environment. Microsoft enforces <a class="lnk" href="nine-power-apps.html">Power Apps licensing</a> more strictly from February 2027.</li> </ul></div> </div> </div> </section> <section class="sec" id="faq" aria-labelledby="fq-h"> <div class="faqsplit"> <div class="faqside rev"> <h2 class="h2" id="fq-h">Dynamics 365 licensing questions we get asked</h2> <p class="lead" style="margin-top:18px">Something else on your mind? Ask us on a call. You get a straight answer, whether or not you work with us.</p> <div class="acts" style="margin-top:24px"><a class="btn btn-p" href="https://www.encloud9.com/lp/schedule-a-meeting/">Book a call</a><a class="lnk" href="nine-faq.html">All questions <span>→</span></a></div> </div> <div> <div class="faq rev"> <details><summary>Can we buy Microsoft licenses from enCloud9?

Yes. enCloud9 sells Microsoft licenses. Ask about them on your call.From Dynamics 365 licensing →

What is a Dynamics 365 attach license?

An attach license adds a second app to a user who already has a base license, at a lower price than a full license. The base must be the highest-priced app that user needs.From Dynamics 365 licensing →

What can a Team Members user do?

View records, enter time and expenses, and update their own items through set apps, with up to 15 tables in a custom app. If a Team Members user starts doing full work, Microsoft expects a full license.From Dynamics 365 licensing →

Do Dynamics 365 users need Power Apps licenses?

Not for apps that extend their licensed Dynamics 365 app in the same environment. Apps used outside that context need Power Apps licensing, and Microsoft enforces this more strictly from February 2027.From Dynamics 365 licensing →

What happens if we run out of storage?

Once a company passes 100% of its storage, Microsoft blocks creating, copying and restoring environments. After 30 days sandboxes go to admin-only mode, and after 90 days sign-in to them is blocked.From Dynamics 365 licensing →

Can you check our licenses?

Yes. Book a call and we go through your users, apps and storage with you, and tell you where you can save or what you are missing. Free checkups, no obligation.From Dynamics 365 licensing →

We will tell you which one fits, even when it is not Dynamics 365.</li> </ul></div> </div> </div> </section> <section class="sec" id="faq" aria-labelledby="fq-h"> <div class="faqsplit"> <div class="faqside rev"> <h2 class="h2" id="fq-h">CRM comparison questions we get asked</h2> <p class="lead" style="margin-top:18px">Something else on your mind? Ask us on a call. You get a straight answer, whether or not you work with us.</p> <div class="acts" style="margin-top:24px"><a class="btn btn-p" href="https://www.encloud9.com/lp/schedule-a-meeting/">Book a call</a><a class="lnk" href="nine-faq.html">All questions <span>→</span></a></div> </div> <div> <div class="faq rev"> <details><summary>Is Dynamics 365 cheaper than Salesforce?

At list price, Dynamics 365 Sales runs $65 to $150 per user per month and Salesforce Sales Cloud $25 to $550. The plans differ in what they include, so compare the plan you would actually need, plus AI and setup.From Dynamics 365 vs Salesforce vs HubSpot →

Is HubSpot free?

HubSpot's Free plan is free for up to 2 users. Paid Sales Hub plans start from $7 per seat per month, and Professional and Enterprise add a one-time onboarding fee of $1,500 or $3,500.From Dynamics 365 vs Salesforce vs HubSpot →

Which CRM works best with Microsoft 365?

Dynamics 365 works inside Outlook and Teams and runs on the same platform as Power Apps and Power BI. Sales Enterprise and Premium include Copilot in Dynamics 365 Sales, Outlook and Teams.From Dynamics 365 vs Salesforce vs HubSpot →

When is Dynamics 365 the wrong choice?

When a very small team wants a free start with no Microsoft 365 in the business, or when a company is deeply invested in another platform and happy with it. We will tell you if that is you.From Dynamics 365 vs Salesforce vs HubSpot →

Can you move us from Salesforce or HubSpot?

Yes. See Move from Salesforce and Move from HubSpot.From Dynamics 365 vs Salesforce vs HubSpot →

Microsoft's contact center app. It routes phone, chat and messaging conversations to the right rep and works with Dynamics 365 Customer Service, with Copilot help for reps.From Contact Center →

How much does Contact Center cost?

Contact Center is $110 per user per month for voice and digital channels, or $95 for Digital or Voice alone, paid yearly. Phone calls are billed separately through Azure Communication Services.From Contact Center →

Do we need Customer Service too?

Contact Center handles the conversations; Customer Service handles cases, queues and knowledge. Customer Service Premium covers both in one plan at $195 per user per month.From Contact Center →

What does Copilot do in Contact Center?

Copilot writes conversation summaries and reply drafts and answers from your knowledge articles. AI self-service agents can handle simple requests before a rep picks up.From Contact Center →

For simpler email marketing on Dynamics 365, ClickDimensions may fit better.</p> <div class="acts" style="margin-top:0"><a class="btn btn-p" href="https://www.encloud9.com/lp/schedule-a-meeting/">Book a call</a></div> </div> <div class="fit rev"> <div class="yes"><h3 class="h3">A good fit if</h3><ul> <li>Customer data sits in several systems that do not match up.</li> <li>You want journeys that react to clicks, visits and purchases.</li> <li>You already have 10 or more Dynamics 365 users, so attach pricing applies.</li> <li>Marketing and sales argue over which list is right. How much does Customer Insights cost?

Customer Insights is $1,700 per company per month, or $1,000 with attach pricing, paid yearly. It includes 100,000 unified people and 10,000 interacted people, with unlimited users.From Customer Insights →

Who qualifies for attach pricing?

Companies with 10 or more users of a qualifying Dynamics 365 app, such as Sales or Customer Service.From Customer Insights →

Customer Insights or ClickDimensions?

Customer Insights suits teams that need one customer view across systems and reactive journeys. ClickDimensions suits simpler email marketing inside Dynamics 365. See marketing automation.From Customer Insights →

class="rev"> <span class="mono">Three forms of AI</span> <h2 class="h2" id="ai-h" style="margin-top:16px">What are the three forms of AI in Dynamics 365?</h2> <p class="lead" style="margin-top:20px">Copilot inside the app, agents Microsoft includes with Dynamics 365, and agents built for your business in Copilot Studio. Copilot is included in the Enterprise and Premium plans, while agents run on Copilot Credits, so we check your data and permissions and estimate the monthly cost before anything is switched on.</p> </div> <nav class="fgx rev" aria-label="The three forms of AI, with examples"> <a class="hd" href="#forms-1"><small>01</small>Copilot in the app</a><a class="hd" href="#agents"><small>02</small>Agents Microsoft includes</a><a class="hd" href="#built"><small>03</small>Agents built for you</a> <a href="#forms-1">Summaries of leads, opportunities and cases</a><a href="#agents">Lead research and outreach drafts</a><a href="#built">Built in Copilot Studio</a> <a href="#forms-1">Email and chat reply drafts</a><a href="#agents">Cases created, updated and closed</a><a href="#built">Published to Teams or your website</a> </nav> </div> <div class="three rev" id="forms-1"> <div><span class="mono">01</span><span class="t">Copilot in the app</span> <span class="d"><b>Sales.</b> Copilot in Dynamics 365 Sales summarizes leads, opportunities and accounts, shows what changed on your records, prepares you for meetings, drafts and summarizes emails, answers questions from your SharePoint documents, and brings you news about your accounts. It only sees records the signed-in person can already open.</span> <span class="d"><b>Customer Service.</b> Copilot in Dynamics 365 Customer Service answers your service reps' questions from your own knowledge sources, summarizes cases and conversations, drafts emails and chat replies, and writes resolution notes. Your reps review every draft before it goes to a customer.</span></div> <div><span class="mono">02</span><span class="t">Agents Microsoft includes</span> <span class="d"><b>Sales.</b> Dynamics 365 Sales includes agents that work on their own: researching leads, watching deals for risk and keeping records up to date.</span> <span class="d"><b>Customer Service.</b> Dynamics 365 Customer Service includes agents that work on their own: creating and updating cases, finding the most common reasons customers get in touch, turning closed cases into knowledge articles, and scoring the quality of cases.</span> <span class="d">We switch on the ones that fit, test them on a small group first, and set a monthly limit on what they can spend.</span></div> <div><span class="mono">03</span><span class="t">Agents built for you</span> <span class="d">For a job only your business has, we build an agent in <a class="lnk" href="nine-copilot-studio.html">Copilot Studio</a> that works on your Dynamics 365 data in Dataverse and can be published to Teams or your website. It is quoted on its own, with its running cost written down.</span></div> </div> <div class="band-foot"> <a class="lnk" href="#agents">See every agent and its status <span>→</span></a> <a class="btn btn-w" href="nine-dynamics-365-sales.html#check">Check if your data is ready</a> </div> </div> </section> <div class="wrap"> <section class="sec" id="agents" aria-labelledby="ag-h"> <div class="sec-head rev"> <h2 class="h2" id="ag-h">Which agents come with Dynamics 365 Sales and Customer Service?</h2> <p class="lead">Microsoft includes agents with both apps. Each one runs on Copilot Credits, and some are still in preview, so we tell you which is which before you decide.</p> </div> <div class="tbl-wrap rev" tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="Table, scrolls sideways on small screens"> <table class="tbl"> <caption class="mono" style="text-align:left;padding-bottom:10px">Agents in Dynamics 365 Sales and Customer Service, checked [publish date]</caption> <thead><tr><th scope="col">Agent</th><th scope="col">What it does</th><th scope="col">Status</th></tr></thead> <tbody> <tr class="grp"><th scope="colgroup" colspan="3">Dynamics 365 Sales</th></tr> <tr><th scope="row"><a class="lnk" href="nine-post-qualification-agent.html">Sales Qualification Agent</a></th><td>Researches assigned leads, checks them against your target customer profile and drafts outreach. In its "research and engage" mode it also emails leads, follows up and hands promising ones to your sellers.</td><td class="sx"><span class="chip ga">Generally available</span></td></tr> <tr><th scope="row">Sales Opportunity Agent</th><td>Pulls CRM data, email, meetings and web research into one deal view, flags risks and shows which deals to focus on.</td><td class="sx"><span class="chip ga">Generally available</span></td></tr> <tr><th scope="row">Sales Research Agent</th><td>Answers business questions about your pipeline in plain language and builds a research report with charts.</td><td class="sx"><span class="chip">[Generally available or preview: confirm the week of publishing]</span></td></tr> <tr><th scope="row">Recommended Actions Agent</th><td>Ranks the next actions from your other agents into one list for each seller.</td><td class="sx"><span class="chip">[Confirm status the week of publishing]</span></td></tr> <tr><th scope="row">AI-powered Data Enrichment</th><td>Reads recent customer emails and Teams meetings and suggests updates to opportunities.</td><td class="sx"><span class="chip ga">Generally available</span></td></tr> <tr><th scope="row">Sales Development agent</th><td>Handles outreach and prospect follow-up from Microsoft Teams. Needs Microsoft 365 Copilot and Microsoft's Agent 365 preview.</td><td class="sx"><span class="chip pv">Preview</span></td></tr> <tr class="grp"><th scope="colgroup" colspan="3">Dynamics 365 Customer Service</th></tr> <tr><th scope="row">Case Management Agent</th><td>Creates, updates, resolves, follows up and closes cases. Fully autonomous case resolution needs an application user and a shared mailbox.</td><td class="sx"><span class="chip ga">Generally available</span></td></tr> <tr><th scope="row">Customer Intent Agent</th><td>Finds the most common reasons customers get in touch from past and current cases and conversations, and suggests new ones.</td><td class="sx"><span class="chip ga">Generally available</span></td></tr> <tr><th scope="row">Customer Knowledge Management Agent</th><td>Reads closed cases and drafts or updates knowledge articles to fill gaps.</td><td class="sx"><span class="chip ga">Generally available</span></td></tr> <tr><th scope="row">Quality Evaluation Agent</th><td>Scores cases against a framework your supervisors set.</td><td class="sx"><span class="chip ga">Generally available</span></td></tr> <tr><th scope="row">Service Agent</th><td>Lets reps find, summarize and update case information from Microsoft 365 Copilot or Copilot Service workspace.</td><td class="sx"><span class="chip ga">Generally available</span></td></tr> </tbody> </table> <p class="fine">Agents run on Copilot Credits. Sales Premium includes 1,000 credits per user per month; other plans buy credits separately. If prepaid credits run out and no pay-as-you-go plan is set, the agents stop until more are added.</p> <p class="fine" style="margin-top:10px">Customer Service Premium includes base credit capacity for the four service agents; other plans buy credits separately. Some agents, including the Case Management and Customer Intent agents, also need a pay-as-you-go plan on an Azure subscription.</p> <p class="fine" style="margin-top:10px">Preview features are not meant for production use. We tell you which is which before you decide.</p> </div> </section> <section class="sec" id="genpages" aria-labelledby="gp-h"> <div class="sec-head rev"> <div> <span class="mono">Generative pages</span> <h2 class="h2" id="gp-h" style="margin-top:16px">Describe the screen. Watch the page build.</h2> </div> <p class="lead">Generative pages let you describe a screen in plain English and get a working page inside a Dynamics 365 app. Microsoft's app agent writes the code and connects it to your Dataverse tables, and you refine it by chatting. This is AI used as a tool to build the report, and we rate it the best use of AI we have seen in a CRM.</p> </div> <div class="gx rev" data-gx> <div class="gx-pick" role="group" aria-label="Pick an example request"> <span class="mono">Pick a request</span> <button type="button" data-pick="a" aria-pressed="true"><span class="g" aria-hidden="true"><i class="d"></i><i class="d"></i><i class="m"></i><i class="d"></i><i class="d"></i><i class="m"></i><i class="on"></i><i class="on"></i><i class="on"></i></span><span class="k">01</span><span class="t">Account 360</span><span class="d">A tab on the account form, before a call.</span></button> <button type="button" data-pick="b" aria-pressed="false"><span class="g" aria-hidden="true"><i class="d"></i><i class="m"></i><i class="m"></i><i class="on"></i><i class="on"></i><i class="on"></i><i class="on"></i><i class="on"></i><i class="on"></i></span><span class="k">02</span><span class="t">Opportunity command center</span><span class="d">The first tab on a deal.</span></button> <button type="button" data-pick="c" aria-pressed="false"><span class="g" aria-hidden="true"><i class="on"></i><i class="on"></i><i class="on"></i><i class="on"></i><i class="on"></i><i class="on"></i><i class="m"></i><i class="m"></i><i class="m"></i></span><span class="k">03</span><span class="t">Approvals</span><span class="d">Quotes waiting for a manager.</span></button> <ol class="gx-how" aria-label="How a generative page is made"> <li><b>Describe it</b><span>Say what the screen should show, in plain English.</span></li> <li><b>The agent builds it</b><span>Microsoft's app agent writes the code and connects it to your Dataverse tables.</span></li> <li><b>Refine by chatting</b><span>Ask for a change and the page updates. A standard form is more consistent and easier to support.</li> <li>You need heavy reporting over a lot of data. Use Power BI.</li> <li>People need to ask questions, not open a screen. Copilot in Dynamics 365 answers questions about your data in a side pane.</li> <li>The need is a conversation or an automated process. Build an agent or workflow in Copilot Studio.</li> <li>You need one control reused across many forms. A PCF code component fits better.</li> <li>Several makers must edit the same page at once. Generative pages do not support co-authoring yet.</li> </ul></div></div> <p class="fine">Also expect to iterate. A new prompt can change parts of the page you were happy with, so test after each change.</p> </div> </div> </section> <section class="sec" id="safe" aria-labelledby="sf-h"> <div class="sec-head rev"> <h2 class="h2" id="sf-h">How do we switch AI on safely?</h2> <p class="lead">Nothing is switched on until your data and permissions are ready and the running cost is written down. class="mono">Agents built for you</span> <h2 class="h2" id="bt-h" style="margin-top:16px">What does an agent built for your business look like?</h2> <p class="lead">For a job only your business has, we build an agent in Copilot Studio that works on your Dynamics 365 data in Dataverse and can be published to Teams or your website. It is quoted on its own, with its running cost written down.</p> <div class="acts" style="margin-top:28px"><a class="btn btn-p" href="https://www.encloud9.com/lp/schedule-a-meeting/">Talk about your agent</a><a class="lnk" href="nine-dynamics-365-sales.html#check">Check if your data is ready <span>→</span></a></div> </div> </div> </section> <section class="sec" id="faq" aria-labelledby="fq-h"> <div class="faqsplit"> <div class="faqside rev"> <h2 class="h2" id="fq-h">Copilot and AI questions we get asked</h2> <p class="lead" style="margin-top:18px">Something else on your mind? Ask us on a call. You get a straight answer on what your data is ready for and what it costs to run.</p> <div class="acts" style="margin-top:24px"><a class="btn btn-p" href="https://www.encloud9.com/lp/schedule-a-meeting/">Book a call</a><a class="lnk" href="tel:+18442640729">1-844-264-0729 <span>→</span></a></div> </div> <div class="faq rev"> <details><summary>Is Copilot included in Dynamics 365 Sales?

Copilot in Dynamics 365 Sales, Outlook and Teams is included in Sales Enterprise and Sales Premium, not in Sales Professional. The Sales agents are available on all three plans but run on Copilot Credits. Only Sales Premium includes credits; on other plans you buy them separately.From Copilot and AI →

What are generative pages in Dynamics 365?

They are pages in model-driven apps that Microsoft's app agent builds from a plain-language description. The agent writes React code that reads and updates your Dataverse data.From Copilot and AI →

Are generative pages generally available?

Yes. Generative pages in model-driven apps are generally available. Using Power Platform connectors and Dataverse custom APIs with them is still in preview.From Copilot and AI →

Does building generative pages cost extra?

Microsoft says the maker experience doesn't require any additional AI or message credits. Users still need a license for the app the page sits in.From Copilot and AI →

Do generative pages replace Power BI or Copilot?

No. Use Power BI for heavy analytics, Copilot for questions about your data, and generative pages for focused working screens.From Copilot and AI →

When does another tool work better than a generative page?

Simple data entry, big reporting over lots of data, or a chat-style need. We will say so in Plan and point you to the better tool.From Copilot and AI →

Ask us on a call. You get a straight answer, whether or not you work with us.</p> <div class="acts" style="margin-top:24px"><a class="btn btn-p" href="https://www.encloud9.com/lp/schedule-a-meeting/">Book a call</a><a class="lnk" href="nine-faq.html">All questions <span>→</span></a></div> </div> <div> <div class="faq rev"> <details><summary>Has enCloud9 built Copilot Studio agents for clients?

Yes. enCloud9 built Copilot Studio chat agents for Compana Pet Brands.From Copilot Studio →

What is Copilot Studio?

Microsoft's tool for building your own AI agents. An agent answers questions from your data and can take actions, such as creating a case or updating a record.From Copilot Studio →

How is Copilot Studio different from Copilot in Dynamics 365?

Copilot in Dynamics 365 Sales and Customer Service comes built in. Copilot Studio is for agents you design for your own business. See Copilot and AI.From Copilot Studio →

How much does Copilot Studio cost?

Microsoft sells Copilot Credits: a pack of 25,000 credits is $200 a month for your whole company, or you can commit up front or pay as you go. Our build work is quoted in writing after a short call.From Copilot Studio →

What uses Copilot Credits?

Each answer or action an agent completes uses a varying number of credits. Agents published to Microsoft 365 Copilot are included for users licensed for Microsoft 365 Copilot.From Copilot Studio →

Can an agent work with our Dynamics 365 data?

Yes. Copilot Studio runs on the same platform as Dynamics 365, so an agent can read and update your records within the security roles you set.From Copilot Studio →

You get a straight answer, whether or not you work with us.</p> <div class="acts" style="margin-top:24px"><a class="btn btn-p" href="https://www.encloud9.com/lp/schedule-a-meeting/">Book a call</a><a class="lnk" href="nine-faq.html">All questions <span>→</span></a></div> </div> <div> <div class="faq rev"> <details><summary>What is Microsoft Power Platform?

Microsoft's low-code family: Power Apps, Power Automate, Power BI, Power Pages and Copilot Studio. It runs on Dataverse, the same data platform as Dynamics 365.From Power Platform →

Do we need Power Platform if we have Dynamics 365?

Dynamics 365 already runs on Power Platform. You add Power Platform tools when you need an app, a workflow, a report or a portal that the Dynamics 365 app does not give you.From Power Platform →

How much does Power Platform cost?

Microsoft prices each tool separately. Power Apps Premium is $20 per user per month, Power Automate Premium is $15, and Power BI Pro is $14, all paid yearly. Our build work is quoted in writing after a short call.From Power Platform →

Which tool should we start with?

Start with the problem. A form or screen your team needs is Power Apps. A manual handoff is Power Automate. A report people build by hand in a spreadsheet is Power BI. A portal for people outside your company is Power Pages.From Power Platform →

Can you build a portal for our clients?

Yes. Power Pages portals sit on the same data as Dynamics 365. See the Collaborative for Children story.From Power Platform →

What about Copilot and agents?

Copilot Studio builds agents on the same data. See Copilot and AI.From Power Platform →

An add-on for Dynamics 365, made by mscrm-addons, that creates documents such as quotes, contracts and reports from your CRM data using Word templates.From Document Core Pack →

Can Document Core Pack send documents for e-signature?

Yes. It works with DocuSign and Adobe Sign, among others. You can set one or more signers and the signing order, and the signed copy is saved back in Dynamics 365.From Document Core Pack →

Which file types can it create?

PDF and Word documents, among other formats. Templates are built in Microsoft Word.From Document Core Pack →

Can it run automatically?

Yes. It can create and send documents in batches, on a schedule, or from a Power Automate flow.From Document Core Pack →

How much does Document Core Pack cost?

mscrm-addons licenses it based on team size and does not publish a single price. Our setup and template work is quoted in writing.From Document Core Pack →

Have you set it up for clients?

Yes. Milestone Leasing creates quotes with it, and PriceMDs uses it with Adobe Sign for e-signatures.From Document Core Pack →

You get a straight answer, whether or not you work with us.</p> <div class="acts" style="margin-top:24px"><a class="btn btn-p" href="https://www.encloud9.com/lp/schedule-a-meeting/">Book a call</a><a class="lnk" href="nine-faq.html">All questions <span>→</span></a></div> </div> <div> <div class="faq rev"> <details><summary>Can Dynamics 365 Sales show Business Central data?

Yes. With Microsoft's integration, sellers see a customer's balance, open invoices and item availability from Business Central while they work in Dynamics 365 Sales.From Business Central integration →

Do you implement Business Central?

enCloud9 focuses on Dynamics 365 and works with a network of Business Central partners for the accounting setup. enCloud9 connects the two systems so they work as one.From Business Central integration →

Does Business Central integrate with Customer Service?

Microsoft's built-in integration is with Dynamics 365 Sales only. Other connections can be built with Power Automate or custom work, quoted in writing.From Business Central integration →

How often does data sync?

Microsoft's default sync jobs run every 30 minutes, and the schedule can be changed. Some updates, like account statistics, can also be run by hand.From Business Central integration →

What does the integration cost?

Our setup work is quoted in writing after a short call. Business Central and Dynamics 365 are licensed separately, and enCloud9 sells Microsoft licenses.From Business Central integration →

Ask us on a call. You get a straight answer, whether or not you work with us.</p> <div class="acts" style="margin-top:24px"><a class="btn btn-p" href="https://www.encloud9.com/lp/schedule-a-meeting/">Book a call</a><a class="lnk" href="nine-faq.html">All questions <span>→</span></a></div> </div> <div> <div class="faq rev"> <details><summary>Has enCloud9 built Power Apps for clients?

Yes. enCloud9 built a Power App for Green Print Partners. Book a call to talk through yours.From Power Apps →

What is Power Apps?

Microsoft's tool for building business apps with little code. Apps run on Dataverse, the same data platform as Dynamics 365, in a browser or on a phone.From Power Apps →

Is Dynamics 365 built on Power Apps?

Yes. Dynamics 365 Sales and Customer Service are model-driven Power Apps. That is why we can add your own screens and forms without moving data anywhere.From Power Apps →

How much does Power Apps cost?

Power Apps Premium is $20 per user per month, paid yearly, or $12 at 2,000 seats or more. The Developer Plan is free for building and testing. Our build work is quoted in writing after a short call.From Power Apps →

Do our Dynamics 365 users need a separate Power Apps license?

Not always. A Dynamics 365 license covers apps that extend that Dynamics 365 app, in the same environment. An app used outside that context needs Power Apps licensing. We check your licenses before you buy anything new.From Power Apps →

What changes in February 2027?

Microsoft starts enforcing Power Apps licensing more strictly. Users of model-driven apps, apps in managed environments and apps used outside a Dynamics 365 environment need a qualifying license, or they cannot open the app. Check your license assignments before then.From Power Apps →

Power Apps or a generative page?

A generative page builds one focused page from a prompt. A Power App is a full app with forms, screens and logic. See generative pages.From Power Apps →

Yes. enCloud9 built Power BI reports for PriceMDs.From Power BI →

What is Power BI?

Microsoft's reporting tool. It connects to Dynamics 365 and many other data sources and turns them into reports and dashboards in a browser or on a phone.From Power BI →

Do we need Power BI if Dynamics 365 has dashboards?

Not always. Dynamics 365 dashboards cover day-to-day pipeline and service views; we built them for BSI and REI. Power BI is for reporting across systems or heavier analysis.From Power BI →

How much does Power BI cost?

Power BI Pro is $14 per user per month and Premium Per User is $24, both paid yearly. A free account works for your own reports. Our build work is quoted in writing after a short call.From Power BI →

Who needs a Power BI license?

Anyone who shares reports, and anyone who views a shared report, needs Pro or Premium Per User, unless your company buys capacity.From Power BI →

Does Copilot replace Power BI?

No. Use Power BI for heavy analytics and Copilot for questions about your data. See Copilot and AI.From Power BI →

Yes. ClickDimensions now goes by Click. Its website describes it as marketing automation for Microsoft CRM, built to integrate natively with Dynamics 365, and its address is still clickdimensions.com.From Marketing →

Should we use Click or Dynamics 365 Customer Insights?

Both run marketing on your Dynamics 365 data. Customer Insights is Microsoft's own app, priced per tenant at $1,700 a month paid yearly, or $1,000 with attach for organizations with 10 or more users of a qualifying Dynamics 365 app. Click is a separate product built for Dynamics 365. We compare both against your list size, channels and budget on a call and tell you which fits.From Marketing →

Does Click work with our website forms?

Yes. Click builds its own forms and landing pages, and its Form Capture connects an existing HTML form on your site, with a separate option for Gravity Forms on WordPress, so submissions reach Dynamics 365.From Marketing →

Can Click email an account, not just a contact?

Yes. Click emails can be sent to account records, to the account's own email address. Click forms and web tracking match people as leads or contacts, not accounts.From Marketing →

Ask us on a call. You get a straight answer, whether or not you work with us.</p> <div class="acts" style="margin-top:24px"><a class="btn btn-p" href="https://www.encloud9.com/lp/schedule-a-meeting/">Book a call</a><a class="lnk" href="tel:+18442640729">1-844-264-0729 <span>→</span></a></div> </div> <div> <div class="faq rev"> <details><summary>How do I start with Email Verifier?

Book a call or ask for the free start. Your first 100 verifications are free, and our team sets Email Verifier up in your Dynamics 365 environment, so you see results on your own records before you pick a plan.From Email Verifier →

Does Email Verifier run inside Dynamics 365?

Yes. Email Verifier is built for Dynamics 365 and runs in your environment. It works with Power Apps, so verification fits the way your team already enters leads and contacts.From Email Verifier →

What is the quality score?

Each address gets a score that ranks its quality, so marketers can put high-value prospects first and hold back addresses that are likely to bounce.From Email Verifier →

What kinds of bad addresses does it catch?

It shows why an address failed: disposable, role-based, defunct or undeliverable. Your team sees the reason on the record, not just a pass or fail.From Email Verifier →

How is this different from the built-in email validation in Dynamics 365?

Built-in validation catches basic problems like bad syntax. Email Verifier checks whether an address can actually receive mail, scores it, and cleans whole lists in bulk.From Email Verifier →

Does it help with ClickDimensions or Customer Insights campaigns?

Yes. Verifying a list before a send cuts bounces in any email platform, including ClickDimensions and Dynamics 365 Customer Insights.From Email Verifier →

What does Email Verifier cost?

Annual plans are $240 for 12,000 verifications, $1,080 for 60,000, or $1,920 for 120,000. You can add verification packs anytime, and the first 100 verifications are free.From Email Verifier →

A Dynamics 365 system that is over-customized or stalled fits Rescue and Repair.From Packages →

Are Microsoft licenses included?

No. Microsoft licenses and Copilot Credits are not part of the package price, and you pay for them separately. As part of setup we assign your licenses to each user and set their security roles, because Microsoft does not let a user open the app until both are done.From Packages →

What if we need more than the package covers?

Anything outside the package is a written change order you approve before work starts. If you need integrations or data from several systems at go-live, a full implementation fits better.From Packages →

full implementation covers everything in your signed scope: configuration of Dynamics 365 Sales, Customer Service or both, data moved from your current CRM or spreadsheets, the integrations you name, training and go-live. Anything not named in the scope, agents and Microsoft licenses are not part of it.</p> </div> <div class="fit two-col rev"> <div class="yes"><h3 class="h3">Included</h3><ul> <li>A written scope from a paid Fit Check, with assumptions and exclusions</li> <li>Configuration of <a class="lnk" href="nine-dynamics-365-sales.html">Sales</a>, and <a class="lnk" href="nine-customer-service.html">Customer Service</a> if in scope</li> <li>Data migration from your current CRM or spreadsheets</li> <li>Integrations named in the scope</li> <li>Your Microsoft licenses assigned to each user</li> <li>Training, go-live and handover to a support plan</li> </ul></div> <div class="no"><h3 class="h3">Not included</h3><ul> <li>Anything not named in the signed scope</li> <li>Agents and Copilot Studio work, scoped separately</li> <li>Microsoft licenses and Copilot Credits</li> </ul></div> </div> <div class="inc-foot rev"> <p class="fine" style="margin-top:0">Anything outside the package is a written change order you approve before work starts.</p> <div class="acts"><span class="ask">Want to know what your project would take?</span><a class="btn btn-p" href="https://www.encloud9.com/lp/schedule-a-meeting/">Book a call to scope it</a></div> </div> </section> <section class="sec" id="fitcheck" aria-labelledby="fc1-h"> <div class="sec-head rev"> <h2 class="h2" id="fc1-h">What is the paid Fit Check?</h2> <p class="lead">The Fit Check is the paid first step of every full implementation: we review your current system and needs, then give you a written scope and a fixed quote for the build. The quote is yours to keep, whether or not you build with us.</p> </div> <div class="three rev"> <div><span class="mono">01 · Review</span><span class="t">Your system and needs</span><span class="d">A review of your current system or need, using our written discovery questionnaire.</span></div> <div><span class="mono">02 · Scope</span><span class="t">A written scope</span><span class="d">A written scope with assumptions, your responsibilities and what is out of scope.</span></div> <div><span class="mono">03 · Quote</span><span class="t">A fixed quote</span><span class="d">A fixed quote for the build, priced per phase.</span></div> </div> <p class="fine rev">Fit Check price: quoted in writing. It is more than you need if this is your first Dynamics 365 Sales or Customer Service system and your process is standard; an accelerator fits that better.</p> <p class="notsure-l">Not sure? Book a call and we will tell you which package fits.</p> <div class="acts" style="margin-top:0"><a class="btn btn-p" href="https://www.encloud9.com/lp/schedule-a-meeting/">Book a call</a></div> </div> <div class="fit rev"> <div class="yes"><h3 class="h3">A good fit if</h3><ul> <li>You need other systems connected to Dynamics 365 on day one.</li> <li>Your data lives in several systems and has to move at go-live.</li> <li>You want Dynamics 365 Sales and Customer Service built together.</li> <li>Your team already works in Outlook and Teams every day.</li> </ul></div> <div class="no"><h3 class="h3">Probably not a fit if</h3><ul> <li>This is your first Dynamics 365 Sales system and your sales process is standard. Ask us on a call. You get a straight answer, whether or not you work with us.</p> <div class="acts" style="margin-top:24px"><a class="btn btn-p" href="https://www.encloud9.com/lp/schedule-a-meeting/">Book a call</a><a class="lnk" href="tel:+18442640729">1-844-264-0729 <span>→</span></a></div> </div> <div> <div class="faq rev"> <details><summary>How much does a full Dynamics 365 implementation cost?

A full implementation starts at $20,000 and is quoted in writing as a fixed price per phase, after a paid Fit Check. Microsoft licenses are a separate cost: Microsoft's list price is $65, $105 or $150 per user per month, paid yearly, for Sales Professional, Enterprise or Premium. Support plans start at $500 a month.From Full implementation →

How long does a Dynamics 365 implementation take?

A full implementation typically takes 8 to 16 weeks, and every project is quoted in writing. You get the plan, with dates, before we build. On our 9 published projects with a delivery time, go-live took 1 to 6 months, and 7 of the 9 took three months or less.From Full implementation →

What is the difference between an accelerator and a full implementation?

Start from where your system is today: a first Dynamics 365 Sales or Customer Service system fits an accelerator, and a system that needs integrations or data from several systems on day one fits a full implementation. A Dynamics 365 system that is over-customized or stalled fits Rescue and Repair.From Full implementation →

What is the paid Fit Check?

The Fit Check is the paid first step of every full implementation: we review your current system and needs, then give you a written scope and a fixed quote for the build. The quote is yours to keep, whether or not you build with us.From Full implementation →

What if our scope changes during the project?

Anything outside the package is a written change order you approve before work starts. Each phase has its own fixed price, so you approve the cost of a change before it is built.From Full implementation →

What are the phases of a Dynamics 365 implementation?

Microsoft's Success by Design framework uses five phases: Discover, Initiate, Implement, Prepare and Operate. Our four stages, Plan, Build, Go live and Run, follow the same path, starting with a written scope from the Fit Check.From Full implementation →

Rescue and Repair runs from $500 for a small fix to $10,000, quoted in writing after we review your system, because every system breaks differently. Microsoft licenses are a separate cost: Microsoft's list price is $65, $105 or $150 per user per month, paid yearly, for Sales Professional, Enterprise or Premium. Support plans start at $500 a month.From Rescue and Repair →

How long does a Dynamics 365 rescue take?

A full rescue typically takes 8 to 16 weeks; a small fix can take days. You get the plan, with dates, before we change anything. Hogan Assessments was back to standard and Tension Envelope back on track, each within three months, and Elmwood Reclaimed Timber moved from on-premises to the cloud within 3 to 4 months.From Rescue and Repair →

Can you fix a Dynamics 365 system another partner built?

Yes. Rescue and Repair takes over systems that are over-customized, stalled or out of date, and takes them back to standard where it can. Tension Envelope's stalled project from a prior partner was back on track within three months.From Rescue and Repair →

Do we have to start over?

No. Rescue and Repair is for Dynamics 365 systems that are over-customized, stalled or out of date. We review it first and tell you what to keep.From Rescue and Repair →

Can you move our on-premises Dynamics CRM to the cloud?

Yes. Moving an on-premises Dynamics system to Dynamics 365 in the cloud can be part of the scope. Elmwood Reclaimed Timber moved its on-premises system to the cloud within 3 to 4 months.From Rescue and Repair →

You get a straight answer, whether or not you work with us.</p> <div class="acts" style="margin-top:24px"><a class="btn btn-p" href="https://www.encloud9.com/lp/schedule-a-meeting/">Book a call</a><a class="lnk" href="tel:+18442640729">1-844-264-0729 <span>→</span></a></div> </div> <div> <div class="faq rev"> <details><summary>What is a Dynamics 365 accelerator?

Our accelerators are fixed-scope packages for a first Dynamics 365 system. You see the scope, price and timeline in writing before we start, and anything outside the package is a written change order you approve first.From Accelerators →

Which accelerator do we need?

The Sales Accelerator is for a team that sells through stages, quotes or products and is starting on Dynamics 365 Sales. The Service Accelerator is for a team that handles customer requests and is starting on Dynamics 365 Customer Service.From Accelerators →

How much does an accelerator cost?

Each accelerator is a fixed $7,500 for our build work. Microsoft licenses are a separate cost, and support plans start at $500 a month.From Accelerators →

Is the Sales Accelerator the same as the sales accelerator in Dynamics 365?

No. Microsoft's sales accelerator is a feature inside Dynamics 365 Sales that gives sellers a prioritized work list and sequences of follow-up steps. Our Sales Accelerator is a package: we build Dynamics 365 Sales for your team to a fixed scope.From Accelerators →

What if we need more than an accelerator covers?

Anything outside the package is a written change order you approve before work starts. If you need integrations or data from several systems at go-live, a full implementation fits better.From Accelerators →

Integrations, agents and Microsoft licenses are not part of it, so the price stays fixed.</p> </div> <div class="fit two-col rev"> <div class="yes"><h3 class="h3">Included</h3><ul> <li><a class="lnk" href="nine-customer-service.html">Dynamics 365 Customer Service</a> configured to how your team handles requests</li> <li>Users and security roles set up</li> <li>Your Microsoft licenses assigned to each user</li> <li>Cases, queues and service levels set up</li> <li>Up to [Brian sets] queues</li> <li>Up to [Brian sets] records imported</li> <li>Up to [Brian sets] custom fields</li> <li>[Brian sets] training sessions</li> <li>[Brian sets] days of help after go-live</li> <li>[Brian sets: knowledge base set up, email to case]</li> </ul></div> <div class="no"><h3 class="h3">Not included</h3><ul> <li>Integrations with other systems, quoted separately</li> <li>Customer Service agents and Copilot Studio agents, built as a separate pilot</li> <li>Voice, live chat and messaging channels, quoted separately</li> <li>Microsoft licenses and Copilot Credits</li> <li>[Brian sets: any of data migration beyond the import limit, custom tables, Power Automate flows]</li> </ul></div> </div> <div class="inc-foot rev"> <p class="fine" style="margin-top:0">Anything outside the package is a written change order you approve before work starts.</p> <div class="acts"><a class="btn btn-p" href="https://www.encloud9.com/lp/schedule-a-meeting/">Ask about the Service Accelerator</a></div> </div> </section> <section class="sec" id="fit" aria-labelledby="fit-h"> <div class="fitsplit"> <div class="side rev"> <h2 class="h2" id="fit-h">Is the Service Accelerator right for your team?</h2> <p class="lead">The Service Accelerator fits a business starting on Dynamics 365 Customer Service for the first time, with customer requests in a shared inbox, spreadsheets or one old help desk tool. It is a weaker fit if you need integrations, phone and chat channels or data from several systems on day one, or if you already have a Dynamics 365 system that is not working.</p> <p class="notsure-l">Not sure? Book a call and we will tell you which package fits.</p> <div class="acts" style="margin-top:0"><a class="btn btn-p" href="https://www.encloud9.com/lp/schedule-a-meeting/">Book a call</a></div> </div> <div class="fit rev"> <div class="yes"><h3 class="h3">A good fit if</h3><ul> <li>This is your first Dynamics 365 Customer Service system.</li> <li>Your team already works in Outlook and Teams every day.</li> <li>Customer requests live in a shared inbox, spreadsheets or a help desk tool nobody trusts.</li> <li>You want every request tracked as a case, with an owner and a response target.</li> <li>Up to [Brian sets] people will use it at go-live.</li> </ul></div> <div class="no"><h3 class="h3">Probably not a fit if</h3><ul> <li>You need other systems connected on day one. A <a class="lnk" href="nine-full-implementation.html">full implementation</a> covers data moves and integrations.</li> <li>You already have a Dynamics 365 Customer Service system that is over-customized or stalled. <a class="lnk" href="nine-rescue-repair.html">Rescue and Repair</a> is built for that.</li> <li>You need phone and chat routing for a contact center on day one. <a class="lnk" href="nine-contact-center.html">Dynamics 365 Contact Center</a> is built for that.</li> </ul></div> </div> </div> </section> <section class="sec" id="process" aria-labelledby="st-h"> <div class="sec-head rev"> <h2 class="h2" id="st-h">How does a Service Accelerator project run?</h2> <p class="lead">Every project runs through the same four stages: Plan, Build, Go live and Run. You see the written plan before we build, and every change after that is written down and approved.</p> </div> <div class="stages flowbar"> <div class="stg"><span class="g" aria-hidden="true"><i class="d" style="--k:0"></i><i style="--k:1"></i><i style="--k:2"></i><i style="--k:3"></i><i style="--k:4"></i><i style="--k:5"></i><i style="--k:6"></i><i style="--k:7"></i><i style="--k:8"></i></span><span class="mono">Stage A</span><span class="t">Plan</span><span class="d">We learn how you serve your customers, using a written discovery questionnaire, and give you the plan: users, queues, service levels, data to move, integrations, and where Copilot and agents fit.</span></div> <div class="stg"><span class="g" aria-hidden="true"><i class="d" style="--k:0"></i><i class="d" style="--k:1"></i><i class="d" style="--k:2"></i><i class="m" style="--k:3"></i><i style="--k:4"></i><i style="--k:5"></i><i style="--k:6"></i><i style="--k:7"></i><i style="--k:8"></i></span><span class="mono">Stage B</span><span class="t">Build</span><span class="d">We build Dynamics 365 Customer Service to the plan, using standard features first, and move your data. You check the imported records against your old system before sign-off.</span></div> <div class="stg"><span class="g" aria-hidden="true"><i class="d" style="--k:0"></i><i class="d" style="--k:1"></i><i class="d" style="--k:2"></i><i class="m" style="--k:3"></i><i class="on" style="--k:4"></i><i class="m" style="--k:5"></i><i style="--k:6"></i><i style="--k:7"></i><i style="--k:8"></i></span><span class="mono">Stage C</span><span class="t">Go live</span><span class="d">Training and cut-over day. Copilot is switched on if your plan includes it; agents are scoped as a separate pilot.</span></div> <div class="stg"><span class="g" aria-hidden="true"><i class="d" style="--k:0"></i><i class="d" style="--k:1"></i><i class="d" style="--k:2"></i><i class="m" style="--k:3"></i><i class="on" style="--k:4"></i><i class="m" style="--k:5"></i><i class="m" style="--k:6"></i><i class="m" style="--k:7"></i><i class="m" style="--k:8"></i></span><span class="mono">Stage D</span><span class="t">Run</span><span class="d">Your support plan starts. Health checks and updates are logged, so you always know what changed.</span></div> </div> </section> <section class="sec" id="stories" aria-labelledby="cs-h"> <div class="sec-head rev"> <h2 class="h2" id="cs-h">Which businesses run Dynamics 365 Customer Service with us?</h2> <p class="lead">Compana Pet Brands in St. Louis has ongoing support from us for Dynamics 365 Sales and Customer Service, and PriceMDs in Clearwater, FL runs Sales and Customer Service on a new Dynamics 365 system that replaced Monday CRM. A move from Salesforce is a fixed price for our work, quoted in writing after a short call. Microsoft licenses are a separate cost: Microsoft's list price is $65, $105 or $150 per user per month, paid yearly, for Sales Professional, Enterprise or Premium. Support plans start at $500 a month.From Move from Salesforce →

How long does a move from Salesforce take?

A move takes [Brian sets] weeks. You get the plan, with dates, before we build.From Move from Salesforce →

Do our Salesforce flows and Apex code move across?

Not on their own. Microsoft's migration tooling reviews flows, Process Builder, workflow rules and Apex code but does not convert them, so they are rebuilt in Dynamics 365. We review them first and quote any rebuild separately.From Move from Salesforce →

Does Microsoft have a tool for moving from Salesforce?

Yes. Microsoft's Dynamics 365 Activate scans a Salesforce org, maps objects and fields to Dynamics 365 Sales and Customer Service, moves the records and checks record counts afterward. It is in preview, and Microsoft says preview features are not meant for production use.From Move from Salesforce →

How long does a move from HubSpot take?

A move takes [Brian sets] weeks. You get the plan, with dates, before we build.From Move from HubSpot →

Do our HubSpot workflows and sequences move across?

Not on their own. Workflows, sequences and connected apps are rebuilt in Dynamics 365 rather than copied. We review them first and quote any rebuild separately.From Move from HubSpot →

Does Microsoft have a tool for moving from HubSpot?

Not a dedicated one. Microsoft's own migration tool, Dynamics 365 Activate, covers moves from Salesforce. For other systems, Microsoft's guidance points to data import, dataflows and data migration tools such as Azure Data Factory.From Move from HubSpot →

A move from Zoho is a fixed price for our work, quoted in writing after a short call. Microsoft licenses are a separate cost: Microsoft's list price is $65, $105 or $150 per user per month, paid yearly, for Sales Professional, Enterprise or Premium. Support plans start at $500 a month.From Move from Zoho →

How long does a move from Zoho take?

A move takes [Brian sets] weeks. You get the plan, with dates, before we build.From Move from Zoho →

Do our Zoho workflows and blueprints move across?

Not on their own. Workflows, blueprints, custom functions and connected apps are rebuilt in Dynamics 365 rather than copied. We review them first and quote any rebuild separately.From Move from Zoho →

Does Microsoft have a tool for moving from Zoho CRM?

Not a dedicated one. Microsoft's own migration tool, Dynamics 365 Activate, covers moves from Salesforce. For other systems, Microsoft's guidance points to data import, dataflows and data migration tools such as Azure Data Factory.From Move from Zoho →

Ask us on a call. You get a straight answer, whether or not you work with us.</p> <div class="acts" style="margin-top:24px"><a class="btn btn-p" href="https://www.encloud9.com/lp/schedule-a-meeting/">Book a call</a><a class="lnk" href="tel:+18442640729">1-844-264-0729 <span>→</span></a></div> </div> <div> <div class="faq rev"> <details><summary>How much does a move from monday.com cost?

A move from monday.com is a fixed price for our work, quoted in writing after a short call. Microsoft licenses are a separate cost: Microsoft's list price is $65, $105 or $150 per user per month, paid yearly, for Sales Professional, Enterprise or Premium. Support plans start at $500 a month.From Move from monday.com →

How long does a move from monday.com take?

A move takes [Brian sets] weeks. You get the plan, with dates, before we build.From Move from monday.com →

Do our monday.com automations and integrations move across?

Not on their own. Automations, integrations and apps are rebuilt in Dynamics 365 rather than copied. We review them first and quote any rebuild separately.From Move from monday.com →

Does Microsoft have a tool for moving from monday.com?

Not a dedicated one. Microsoft's own migration tool, Dynamics 365 Activate, covers moves from Salesforce. For other systems, Microsoft's guidance points to data import, dataflows and data migration tools such as Azure Data Factory.From Move from monday.com →

Which support plan fits our team?

Optimization is built for teams of up to 50 users and Partnership for 50 users and up. Stability gives 4 hours a month for teams that need steady break and fix help, enhancements and user management.From Support plans →

What does the 1-hour response mean?

On monthly plans, a person picks up your request within 1 hour during business hours, 7:00am to 5:00pm Central, Monday to Friday. It means the request has been picked up and reviewed, not that it is solved.From Support plans →

Is there a setup or onboarding fee?

New clients pay an onboarding fee of up to one month's charge.From Support plans →

What happens if we need more hours?

Optimization includes add-on hour blocks, and Partnership includes discounted add-on hours. On-Demand work is $200 an hour.From Support plans →

Can you support a Dynamics 365 system another partner built?

Yes. If the system needs repair first, Rescue and Repair gets it working, then a support plan keeps it that way.From Support plans →

<section class="sec" id="faq" aria-labelledby="faq-h"> <div class="faqsplit"> <div class="faqside rev"> <span class="mono">Questions we hear</span> <h2 class="h2" id="faq-h" style="margin-top:16px">Dataverse storage questions</h2> <p class="lead" style="margin-top:20px">Still not sure where you stand? The analysis answers these for your own tenant.</p> <a class="btn btn-p" href="#book" style="margin-top:28px">Book my free storage analysis</a> </div> <div class="faq rev"> <details><summary>What happens when we go over our Dataverse storage limit?

Once Microsoft's rollout reaches your tenant: from the day you go over, you cannot create, copy, restore or recover environments. After 30 days, sandbox environments are limited to administrators. After 90 days, nobody can sign in to them, admins included.From Dataverse storage →

What messages will we see from Microsoft?

Warning emails, plus banners in the Power Platform admin center, the maker portals and your Dynamics 365 apps. They start when less than 15% of your database, file or log storage is left, get stronger below 5%, and continue once you are over. Admins and makers get the emails every week.From Dataverse storage →

Will Dynamics 365 CRM stop working?

No. Your production apps keep running. What is blocked is anything that needs a restore, a copy or a test environment.From Dataverse storage →

Can we turn off Microsoft's storage warning emails or notifications?

No. Once you are near or over the limit, admins get the emails every week, with no way to opt out. A banner you dismiss stays hidden for seven days, then comes back if you are still over.From Dataverse storage →

Which storage type is my warning about?

Dataverse storage splits into database, file and log. You can see the split in the Power Platform admin center under Licensing, then Dataverse. The free analysis checks this for you.From Dataverse storage →

How much does extra Dataverse storage cost?

Extra database storage can cost up to $500 per GB a year.From Dataverse storage →

Should we buy more storage or clean up our data?

It depends which storage type is over and what is using it. Database storage is expensive, so a cleanup often pays for itself. The analysis recommends one or both.From Dataverse storage →

What takes up the most Dataverse storage?

Usually old emails and attachments, notes, audit history, system logs and environments nobody uses. The analysis finds the biggest tables and the fastest-growing ones.From Dataverse storage →

What is the free Dataverse Storage Analysis?

A one-hour Teams meeting with an enCloud9 consultant. We find what is using your storage and how fast it is growing, then work with you on a plan to get back under your limit. It is free and open to any organization.From Dataverse storage →
